# BAD-040 — Guard release-note art bytes against art.lock.json in npm test

## Brief
No test covers scripts/build-release-notes-art.js. A change to a shared SVG primitive (after BAD-036, scripts/release-notes-art/svg.js, motion.js or constants.js) silently changes every published illustration's SVG bytes. Nothing notices until someone runs npm run release-notes:render, usually mid-release, and it re-encodes already-published GIFs on whatever ffmpeg is installed (8.0 and 8.1 differ by 384 bytes). A pure-Node test that copies scripts/ to a temp root, runs the generator there and compares each output's digest with docs/release-notes/art.lock.json would catch this at PR time, in milliseconds, without Electron.

Evidence: grep -rn build-release-notes-art test/ finds only a comment (test/fonts.test.js:65). The digest recipe is reproducible in plain Node (scripts/render-release-notes.js:60-72, 137-146). Measured at 20d11e1: 12 of 12 lock entries match a fresh generation in a scratch copy. Spike: spud:docs/spikes/bad-036/scripts-release-notes-art.md §8 check 3 and §10.
